summary: Solved in July 2026. OpenAI announced a proof, produced by GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, that every bridgeless graph has a cycle double cover; Sang-il Oum's arXiv exposition (arXiv:2607.16356) presents it in a self-contained form suitable for advanced undergraduates, assuming only Fleischner's splitting lemma and the Nash-Williams--Tutte tree-packing theorem. The proof reduces to cubic 3-edge-connected graphs, takes a nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$-flow $\phi$ (Jaeger, Kilpatrick), and shows via an $\mathbb{F}_2$ consistency criterion (solvability of $At=b$, checked through $C(A)=\ker(A^{T})^{\perp}$) that vertex labels $t_v$ exist for which the two-element edge label $P_e = t_u+\phi(f_u)+\langle\phi(e)\rangle$ is well defined; the supports of the seven nonzero labels are Eulerian and cover every edge exactly twice. The argument yields an 8-cycle double cover. The 5-cycle double cover conjecture, the orientable/directed cycle double cover conjecture, the general strong embedding conjecture and the Berge-Fulkerson conjecture all remain open.

since_posted.authors: OpenAI (proof produced by GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra)
since_posted.claim: Announced (11 July 2026) a complete proof that every bridgeless graph has a cycle double cover, settling the conjecture of Seymour and Szekeres. The argument reduces to cubic 3-edge-connected graphs, starts from a nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$-flow, and uses an $\mathbb{F}_2$ linear-algebra consistency criterion to choose a two-element label set for every edge; the supports of the labels form the cover.

since_posted.title: A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture by OpenAI: An exposition
since_posted.claim: Self-contained ~10-page exposition of the OpenAI proof, assuming only Fleischner's splitting lemma and the Nash-Williams--Tutte tree-packing theorem. Symmetrises the choice of the two edge labels and replaces the dual-space argument by the identity $C(A)=\ker(A^{T})^{\perp}$. Also records the consequences: an 8-cycle double cover for every bridgeless graph, the strong (circular) embedding conjecture for cubic graphs, Bondy's small cycle double cover conjecture for simple 2-connected cubic graphs $\ne K_4$ (via Lai--Yu--Zhang), and the Jamshy--Tarsi matroid form.

since_posted.title: Directed Cycle Double Cover Conjecture: Fork Graphs
since_posted.claim: Proves Jaeger's directed cycle double cover conjecture for lean fork-graphs, an inductively defined class of cubic bridgeless graphs whose members contain subdivisions of all cubic bridgeless graphs as induced subgraphs.

since_posted.title: Counting circuit double covers
since_posted.claim: Proves an exponential lower bound on the number of circuit double covers for planar bridgeless cubic graphs and an almost-exponential lower bound for graphs with surface embedding representativity at least 4, establishing the first counting results toward CDC.

since_posted.title: Approximate cycle double cover
since_posted.claim: Establishes nontrivial upper bounds on the minimum number of singular edges in a 2-cell embedding of a cubic graph (CDC being equivalent to achieving zero singular edges), giving an approximate version of the conjecture with efficient algorithms.

since_posted.title: Facial diagrams and cycle double cover
since_posted.claim: Studies circular 2-cell embeddings of cubic graphs via twist operations on edges, derives bounds on singular edges, and develops analytical tools further advancing the approximate CDC program.

notes: Status changed partial -> solved on 2026-09-06 on the strength of arXiv:2607.16356v3 (Oum, 1 Aug 2026), an exposition of the proof announced by OpenAI on 11 July 2026. Caveat: neither the announcement nor the exposition has been peer-reviewed or journal-published yet, and the earlier arXiv claims (1202.0569, 1510.02075, 1811.08719) are a reminder that CDC attracts flawed proofs. What is different here is that the write-up is short, elementary and checkable by hand -- it cites only Fleischner's splitting lemma and the Nash-Williams--Tutte tree-packing theorem -- and that the exposition is by a recognised expert (Sang-il Oum, IBS Discrete Mathematics Group), who states it as Theorem 1 and derives further consequences from it. Downstream consequences recorded in the exposition: (i) Theorem 18, every bridgeless graph has an 8-cycle double cover, which fills the (8,2) box of the (m,n)-cycle-cover chart; (ii) the strong/circular embedding conjecture now holds for cubic graphs (Jaeger's survey reduction), though it stays open in general; (iii) Corollary 17, Bondy's small cycle double cover conjecture for simple 2-connected cubic graphs other than $K_4$ becomes unconditional via Lai-Yu-Zhang; (iv) Theorem 27, the Jamshy-Tarsi equivalence upgrades to a theorem: every binary matroid with no coloop and no $F_7^{*}$-minor has a cycle double cover, hence so does every coloop-free regular matroid. Explicitly NOT settled: Bondy's $n-1$ small CDC conjecture for simple 2-edge-connected graphs, the 5-cycle double cover conjecture (Celmins, Preissmann), the orientable 5-CDC conjecture (Archdeacon, Jaeger) which would imply the 5-flow conjecture, the oriented cycle double cover conjecture stated further down this OPG page, and Berge-Fulkerson. The timeline start year is pinned to 1973 (Szekeres, Polyhedral decompositions of cubic graphs, for bridgeless cubic graphs; Seymour stated the general bridgeless form in 1979) via the review's `claim_year` field: the bibliography heuristic would otherwise date the bar from Tutte 1954, a cited antecedent rather than the conjecture.
